sections.title: What is Prefix Sum?
sections.content:
Prefix sum is one of the simplest yet most powerful array preprocessing techniques in DSA. The idea: build a `prefix` array where `prefix[i]` stores the cumulative sum of `arr[0]` through `arr[i-1]`. Once built, any range sum query `arr[l..r]` can be answered in O(1) as `prefix[r+1] - prefix[l]`. Preprocessing takes O(n); each query is O(1). This transforms problems requiring many subarray sum queries from O(n²) to O(n).

The technique extends naturally beyond 1D. A **2D prefix sum** enables O(1) rectangle sum queries over a matrix. A **prefix XOR** array enables O(1) range XOR queries. A **difference array** (the inverse of prefix sum) enables O(1) range updates followed by a single O(n) reconstruction pass.

Prefix sum also combines powerfully with **hash maps** for subarray counting problems. The pattern 'count subarrays with sum exactly k' cannot be solved efficiently with just a prefix array - but pairing prefix sums with a frequency map reduces it from O(n²) to O(n). This combination is one of the most common patterns in medium-hard array problems.

Prefix sum should be learned early - it applies across arrays, matrices, strings, and graphs. It is not a standalone algorithm but a building block that eliminates repeated range computation throughout a solution.

sections.title: When to Use This
sections.content: Use prefix sum when you need to answer multiple range sum (or range XOR) queries over a static array efficiently. Use the prefix sum + hash map pattern when counting subarrays or subsequences with a specific sum, product, or XOR. Use difference arrays when you need to apply multiple range update operations followed by a single read pass. Use 2D prefix sums for rectangle sum queries over a matrix. If the array changes between queries, use a Fenwick Tree or Segment Tree instead.

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
## 1D Prefix Sum

Build a 1-indexed prefix array of size `n + 1`:
- `prefix[0] = 0` (empty prefix - no elements)
- `prefix[i] = prefix[i-1] + arr[i-1]` for i from 1 to n

Range sum of `arr[l..r]` (0-indexed): `prefix[r+1] - prefix[l]`.

The convention of making prefix size `n+1` with `prefix[0] = 0` eliminates special cases - the query formula works uniformly even when `l = 0`.

## Prefix Sum + Hash Map for Subarray Problems

To **count subarrays with sum exactly k**: iterate through the array maintaining a running sum. At each position, check how many previous running sums equal `runningSum - k`. If they do, the subarray between that earlier position and the current one has sum exactly k.

Implementation: maintain a hash map `countMap` where `countMap[s]` is how many times running sum `s` has appeared. Before iterating, initialize `countMap[0] = 1` - this accounts for subarrays starting at index 0. For each element: `runningSum += arr[i]`, then `result += countMap[runningSum - k] || 0`, then `countMap[runningSum] = (countMap[runningSum] || 0) + 1`.

**Why `{0: 1}`**: if `runningSum === k` at some position, we need `countMap[0]` to exist. Without it, subarrays from the start are missed.

## Difference Arrays for Range Updates

A difference array `diff` where `diff[i] = arr[i] - arr[i-1]` (with `diff[0] = arr[0]`) encodes the array as its own differences. A range update 'add v to all elements in [l, r]' becomes just two point updates: `diff[l] += v` and `diff[r+1] -= v` (if `r+1 <= n`). Reconstruct the updated array by taking the prefix sum of `diff`. O(1) per update, O(n) for final reconstruction.

## 2D Prefix Sum

For an m×n matrix, build `prefix[i][j]` = sum of all elements in the rectangle from `(0,0)` to `(i-1, j-1)` (1-indexed prefix, 0-indexed matrix). Build formula using inclusion-exclusion:
```
prefix[i][j] = mat[i-1][j-1] + prefix[i-1][j] + prefix[i][j-1] - prefix[i-1][j-1]
```
Rectangle sum from `(r1, c1)` to `(r2, c2)` (0-indexed):
```
prefix[r2+1][c2+1] - prefix[r1][c2+1] - prefix[r2+1][c1] + prefix[r1][c1]
```
The `+ prefix[r1][c1]` at the end corrects for the corner being subtracted twice.

sections.title: Core Template
sections.explanation: Three core prefix sum patterns in one template: standard 1D prefix for range queries, prefix+hashmap for subarray count problems, and difference array for range updates. Each solves a distinct class of problems with O(n) preprocessing and O(1) or O(Q) total query cost.

items.name: XOR Prefix Sum
items.description: Replace addition with XOR: `prefixXor[i] = prefixXor[i-1] ^ arr[i-1]`. Range XOR of `[l, r]` is `prefixXor[r+1] ^ prefixXor[l]` - works because XOR is its own inverse. O(1) per range XOR query after O(n) build.

items.name: Difference Array
items.description: Inverse of prefix sum. Store differences between adjacent elements. Range updates become two point updates. Reconstruct the final array with a single prefix sum pass. Optimal when you have many range updates followed by a single read.

items.name: 2D Prefix Sum
items.description: Extend prefix sums to matrices for O(1) rectangle sum queries. Build using inclusion-exclusion in O(m*n). Query uses the 4-corner formula. Useful for sub-matrix sum problems and 2D sliding window problems.

items.name: Sparse Table (Range Min/Max)
items.description: For static arrays, build a sparse table in O(n log n) to answer range min/max queries in O(1). Unlike prefix sums, it uses the overlap-friendly property of min/max (overlapping ranges give the same result). Best for heavy min/max query workloads without updates.

sections.title: Complexity
sections.time: O(n) build, O(1) per range query
sections.explanation: Building the prefix array makes one pass over the input: O(n). Each range sum query is a single subtraction: O(1). For Q queries over an array of size n: O(n + Q) total, versus O(nQ) for naive per-query summation. 2D prefix sum: O(m*n) build, O(1) per rectangle query. Difference array: O(1) per update, O(n) for final reconstruction - optimal when updates >> reads. Prefix+hashmap subarray counting: O(n) time, O(n) space for the hash map.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Off-by-one in index: `prefix[i]` stores the sum of the first `i` elements (not including index i of the original array). Range `[l, r]` (0-indexed) sum is `prefix[r+1] - prefix[l]`, not `prefix[r] - prefix[l-1]` - these are equivalent but the latter breaks when `l = 0` (negative index).
Prefix+hashmap: not initializing `countMap.set(0, 1)` before iterating - this misses all subarrays starting at index 0 where the prefix sum exactly equals k. The empty prefix must be pre-seeded.

2D prefix sum: forgetting to add back the top-left corner in the query formula - `prefix[r2+1][c2+1] - prefix[r1][c2+1] - prefix[r2+1][c1] + prefix[r1][c1]`. The minus-minus double-subtracts the top-left rectangle; the final `+ prefix[r1][c1]` corrects this.
Difference array: applying `diff[r+1] -= v` without checking `r+1 <= n` - writing to `diff[n+1]` when `r = n-1` is out of bounds. Always guard the right boundary.
Using prefix sum when the array has updates between queries - prefix sums are static. For dynamic arrays with interleaved updates and queries, use a Fenwick Tree or Segment Tree.

items.title: Range Sum Query - Immutable
items.why: The canonical 1D prefix sum problem - build prefix array once, answer all range sum queries in O(1).

items.title: Subarray Sum Equals K
items.why: The canonical prefix sum + hash map problem - count subarrays with exact sum using running sum and frequency map.

items.title: Product of Array Except Self
items.why: Tests applying the prefix sum pattern to products - build prefix product array and suffix product array, combine for O(n) O(1)-space solution.

items.title: Number of Ways to Split Array
items.why: Tests prefix sum for comparing left and right subarray sums at each split point - direct application of prefix array for multiple range queries.

sections.title: What to Learn Next
sections.why: Monotonic Stack is the next Others topic. Like prefix sum, it is a linear-time preprocessing technique - but for 'next greater/smaller element' problems. Many problems combine prefix sums and monotonic stacks, so learning both back-to-back builds the pattern library quickly.
